q: How many Availability Zones can Amazon EFS store data across within a region?

exp.a: Incorrect. EFS stores data across multiple AZs for high availability (EFS One Zone stores in 1 AZ).
exp.b: Incorrect. Standard EFS stores data across 3 or more AZs in a region.
exp.c: Correct. EFS Standard storage class stores data redundantly across multiple (3+) AZs.
exp.d: Incorrect. EFS is a regional service that spans multiple AZs.

q: What is the maximum storage capacity of Amazon EFS?

opts.c: No pre-provisioned limit – scales to petabytes automatically

exp.a: Incorrect. 16 TB is the max size of a single EBS volume, not EFS.
exp.b: Incorrect. EFS has no fixed storage limit of 64 TB.
exp.c: Correct. EFS automatically scales up to petabytes without pre-provisioning.
exp.d: Incorrect. EFS can scale to petabytes but it grows and shrinks automatically.

q: How many EC2 instances can concurrently connect to a single Amazon EFS file system?

exp.a: Incorrect. EFS is designed for shared access across many instances.
exp.b: Incorrect. EFS supports far more than 10 instances.
exp.c: Incorrect. EFS can handle more than 100 concurrent connections.
exp.d: Correct. EFS supports thousands of concurrent EC2 instance connections.

q: What is the cost savings percentage when using EFS Infrequent Access compared to EFS Standard?

exp.a: Incorrect. The savings are much higher than 50%.
exp.b: Incorrect. The savings can be higher than 72%.
exp.c: Correct. EFS IA can provide up to 92% lower cost compared to EFS Standard.
exp.d: Incorrect. The savings are significantly more than 30%.

q: After how many days of not being accessed can a file be moved to EFS IA using Lifecycle Management?

exp.a: Correct. EFS Lifecycle policies can be set to 7, 14, 30, 60, or 90 days.
exp.b: Incorrect. Multiple lifecycle policy durations are available.
exp.c: Incorrect. 1 day is not a valid lifecycle policy duration for EFS.
exp.d: Incorrect. There are more options than just 60 or 90 days.

q: What is the maximum throughput per file system in EFS Bursting Throughput mode for Standard storage?

exp.a: Correct. In Bursting mode, throughput scales at 50 MiB/s per TiB baseline and bursts to 100 MiB/s per TiB.
exp.b: Incorrect. 50 MiB/s per TiB is the baseline, but burst can reach 100 MiB/s per TiB.
exp.c: Incorrect. 250 MiB/s is not the burst rate per TiB.
exp.d: Incorrect. 1 GiB/s per TiB is not the correct burst throughput.

q: What is the default baseline throughput in EFS Bursting mode per TiB of Standard storage?

exp.a: Incorrect. 100 MiB/s is the burst throughput, not the baseline.
exp.b: Correct. The baseline throughput in Bursting mode is 50 MiB/s per TiB of storage.
exp.c: Incorrect. 25 MiB/s is not the correct baseline.
exp.d: Incorrect. 150 MiB/s is not the correct baseline throughput.

q: Which port must be open in the security group for EC2 instances to mount an EFS file system?

exp.a: Incorrect. Port 80 is for HTTP traffic, not NFS.
exp.b: Incorrect. Port 443 is for HTTPS, not NFS.
exp.c: Correct. Port 2049 must be open for NFS traffic to mount EFS.
exp.d: Incorrect. Port 22 is for SSH access, not for mounting EFS.

q: How many mount targets can you create per Availability Zone for an EFS file system?

exp.a: Incorrect. There is a limit of one mount target per AZ.
exp.b: Correct. You can create one mount target per Availability Zone for a standard EFS file system.
exp.c: Incorrect. Only 1 mount target per AZ is allowed.
exp.d: Incorrect. Only 1 mount target per AZ is allowed.

q: What is the maximum file size supported in Amazon EFS?

exp.a: Incorrect. 5 TB is the max object size in S3.
exp.b: Correct. The maximum individual file size in EFS is 47.9 TiB.
exp.c: Incorrect. 16 TB is the max EBS volume size.
exp.d: Incorrect. 52.2 TiB is not the correct maximum file size.

q: What is the maximum number of file systems you can create per AWS account per region (default)?

exp.a: Incorrect. The default limit is higher than 10.
exp.b: Incorrect. The default limit is higher than 100.
exp.c: Correct. The default limit is 1,000 EFS file systems per account per region.
exp.d: Incorrect. 1,000,000 is far too high.

q: How much cost savings does EFS One Zone provide compared to EFS Standard?

exp.a: Incorrect. The savings are higher than 25%.
exp.b: Correct. EFS One Zone provides up to 47% savings compared to EFS Standard.
exp.c: Incorrect. 75% is not the correct savings figure.
exp.d: Incorrect. 90% is not the correct savings for One Zone vs Standard.

q: What is the availability SLA for EFS Standard storage class?

exp.a: Incorrect. 99.9% is not the SLA for EFS Standard.
exp.b: Correct. EFS Standard offers 99.99% availability.
exp.c: Incorrect. 99.999% is not the advertised SLA.
exp.d: Incorrect. 99.95% is not the EFS Standard SLA.

q: What is the availability SLA for EFS One Zone storage class?

exp.a: Incorrect. 99.99% is for EFS Standard.
exp.b: Correct. EFS One Zone offers 99.9% availability (lower than Standard due to single AZ).
exp.c: Incorrect. 99.95% is not the One Zone SLA.
exp.d: Incorrect. 99.5% is not the correct SLA.

q: What is the approximate cost of EFS Standard storage per GB per month (US East region)?

exp.a: Correct. EFS Standard storage costs approximately $0.30 per GB per month.
exp.b: Incorrect. $0.08 is closer to EBS pricing, not EFS Standard.
exp.c: Incorrect. $0.023 is the cost of S3 Standard storage, not EFS.
exp.d: Incorrect. $0.50 is too high for EFS Standard.

q: What is the approximate cost of EFS Infrequent Access storage per GB per month?

exp.a: Incorrect. $0.30 is the EFS Standard price.
exp.b: Correct. EFS IA costs approximately $0.025/GB/month for storage plus per-access charges.
exp.c: Incorrect. $0.10 is not the correct IA pricing.
exp.d: Incorrect. $0.005 is too low; that's closer to Glacier pricing.

q: What is the RPO (Recovery Point Objective) for EFS Replication?

exp.a: Incorrect. 24 hours is too long; EFS Replication has a shorter RPO.
exp.b: Correct. EFS Replication is designed to provide an RPO of 15 minutes for most file systems.
exp.c: Incorrect. 1 hour is longer than the typical EFS Replication RPO.
exp.d: Incorrect. While some replications may be faster, the designed RPO is 15 minutes.

q: What is the durability of Amazon EFS Standard storage class?

exp.a: Incorrect. 99.9% is far lower than EFS durability.
exp.b: Incorrect. 99.99% is the availability SLA, not durability.
exp.c: Correct. EFS Standard is designed for 99.999999999% (11 nines) durability.
exp.d: Incorrect. EFS provides 11 nines of durability.

q: What is the maximum throughput achievable with EFS in Elastic Throughput mode for reads?

exp.a: Incorrect. EFS Elastic mode can achieve higher read throughput.
exp.b: Incorrect. 3 GiB/s is the write throughput limit.
exp.c: Correct. EFS Elastic Throughput mode supports up to 10 GiB/s for reads.
exp.d: Incorrect. 5 GiB/s is not the maximum read throughput.

q: What is the maximum write throughput in EFS Elastic Throughput mode?

exp.a: Incorrect. 1 GiB/s is lower than the actual maximum.
exp.b: Correct. EFS Elastic Throughput supports up to 3 GiB/s for writes.
exp.c: Incorrect. 10 GiB/s is the read throughput maximum.
exp.d: Incorrect. 5 GiB/s is not the write throughput maximum.

q: A development team has an EFS file system with 500 GiB of data in Bursting Throughput mode. What is the baseline throughput available?

exp.a: Incorrect. 50 MiB/s would be the baseline for 1 TiB of storage.
exp.b: Correct. Baseline throughput is 50 MiB/s per TiB. For 500 GiB (0.5 TiB), baseline = 50 × 0.5 = 25 MiB/s.
exp.c: Incorrect. 100 MiB/s would be the burst for 1 TiB.
exp.d: Incorrect. 12.5 MiB/s would be for 250 GiB.

q: An EFS file system has 2 TiB of data in Bursting Throughput mode. What is the maximum burst throughput?

exp.a: Incorrect. 100 MiB/s is the burst for 1 TiB.
exp.b: Correct. Burst throughput = 100 MiB/s per TiB × 2 TiB = 200 MiB/s.
exp.c: Incorrect. 300 MiB/s would require 3 TiB of data.
exp.d: Incorrect. 50 MiB/s is the baseline for 1 TiB, not the burst for 2 TiB.

q: What is the maximum number of EFS access points you can create per file system?

exp.a: Incorrect. The limit is much higher than 10.
exp.b: Incorrect. The limit is higher than 50.
exp.c: Incorrect. 120 was an older limit that has been increased.
exp.d: Correct. You can create up to 1,000 access points per EFS file system.

q: What is the minimum burst throughput guaranteed for all EFS file systems in Bursting mode, regardless of size?

exp.a: Incorrect. All EFS file systems can burst to at least 100 MiB/s.
exp.b: Correct. Regardless of file system size, EFS guarantees a minimum burst throughput of 100 MiB/s.
exp.c: Incorrect. The minimum burst is higher than 10 MiB/s.
exp.d: Incorrect. The guaranteed minimum burst is 100 MiB/s.

q: What is the per-access charge for reading data from EFS Infrequent Access storage class?

exp.a: Correct. EFS IA charges approximately $0.01 per GB of data read/written when accessing IA files.
exp.b: Incorrect. $0.03 per GB is not the correct per-access rate.
exp.c: Incorrect. $0.06 per GB is too high.
exp.d: Incorrect. There is a per-access charge for IA data.

q: What is the maximum transfer speed that AWS DataSync can achieve?

exp.a: Incorrect. DataSync can achieve higher speeds than 1 Gbps.
exp.b: Correct. AWS DataSync can transfer data at speeds up to 10 Gbps per task.
exp.c: Incorrect. 100 Mbps is far below DataSync capabilities.
exp.d: Incorrect. DataSync can exceed 5 Gbps.

q: Which of the following is TRUE about EFS General Purpose mode IOPS?

opts.a: It supports up to 35,000 read IOPS and 7,000 write IOPS per file system
opts.d: IOPS scales with storage size like EBS gp3

exp.a: Correct. EFS General Purpose mode supports up to 35,000 read IOPS and 7,000 write IOPS.
exp.b: Incorrect. There are IOPS limits in General Purpose mode (use Max I/O for higher).
exp.c: Incorrect. 3,000 IOPS baseline is for EBS gp3, not EFS.
exp.d: Incorrect. EFS IOPS limits are per file system and don't scale with storage size in the same way as EBS.

q: What is the IOPS capability of EFS Max I/O performance mode?

exp.a: Incorrect. 35,000 is the read IOPS limit for General Purpose mode.
exp.b: Correct. Max I/O mode can scale to 500,000+ IOPS for highly parallelized applications.
exp.c: Incorrect. 7,000 is the write IOPS limit for General Purpose mode.
exp.d: Incorrect. Max I/O can exceed 100,000 IOPS.

q: A company has 50 TiB in EFS Standard with Bursting Throughput. What is their baseline throughput?

exp.a: Correct. Baseline = 50 MiB/s per TiB × 50 TiB = 2,500 MiB/s.
exp.b: Incorrect. 5,000 MiB/s would be the burst throughput (100 × 50).
exp.c: Incorrect. 500 MiB/s would be baseline for 10 TiB.
exp.d: Incorrect. 1,000 MiB/s would be baseline for 20 TiB.

q: A company is evaluating costs. They have 10 TiB in EFS Standard ($0.30/GB/month) and 40 TiB in EFS Standard-IA ($0.025/GB/month). What is their approximate monthly storage cost?

exp.b: Incorrect. IA cost calculation is wrong.
exp.c: Incorrect. The Standard and IA cost values are swapped.
exp.d: Incorrect. These calculations don't match the given pricing.

q: What is the maximum Provisioned Throughput value you can configure for a single EFS file system without requesting a limit increase?

exp.a: Incorrect. You can provision higher than 256 MiB/s.
exp.b: Incorrect. You can provision higher than 512 MiB/s.
exp.c: Correct. The default maximum for Provisioned Throughput is 1 GiB/s (1,024 MiB/s). Higher requires a limit increase request.
exp.d: Incorrect. 3 GiB/s is the Elastic mode write throughput maximum.

q: What is the total number of EFS storage classes available?

exp.a: Incorrect. There are more than 2 storage classes when including One Zone variants.
exp.b: Correct. EFS has 4 storage classes: Standard, Standard-IA, One Zone, and One Zone-IA.
exp.c: Incorrect. There are 4 storage classes (EFS Archive was added later as a 5th, but traditionally 4).
exp.d: Incorrect. There are 4 main storage classes, not 3.
